result.topic_en: The page ends an argument on prime-counting inequalities involving π(q_r) − π(p_r) and log q_r, then states a theta-function identity expressing a ratio of f(x,y) series, times the cube of an infinite product, as a Lambert-type series.
result.transcription:
$\{\pi(q_r) - \pi(p_r)\}\log q_r \geqslant \{\pi(p_s) - \pi(q_s)\}\log q_s$
or $\qquad n\log q_r \geqslant \left[\frac{n\log(1+\frac{1}{r})}{\log(1+\frac{1}{s})}\right]\log q_s .$
Now we have to express $q_r$ and $q_s$ in terms of $p_r$ and $p_s$ respectively.

$f(x,y) = 1 + x(y+\frac{1}{y}) + x^4(y^2+\frac{1}{y^2}) + x^9(y^3+\frac{1}{y^3}) + \cdots .$

$\frac{f(\sqrt{ab},\, n\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}})}{n\, f(-\sqrt{ab},\, -\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}})\, f(\sqrt{ab},\, n\sqrt{ab})}\{(1-ab)(1-a^2b^2)(1-a^3b^3)\cdots\}^3$

$= \frac{1}{1+n} + \left(\frac{a}{n+ab} + \frac{b}{1+nab}\right) + \left(\frac{a^2}{n+a^2b^2} + \frac{b^2}{1+na^2b^2}\right)$
$+ \left(\frac{a^3}{n+a^3b^3} + \frac{b^3}{1+na^3b^3}\right) + \cdots$

methods.what: Inequality between prime-counting differences weighted by logarithms
Definition of a two-variable theta series f(x,y)
Identity expressing a quotient of theta functions times a cubed infinite product as a Lambert-type series (partial fraction expansion)

items.english: Now we have to express q_r and q_s in terms of p_r and p_s respectively.
The quotient of theta functions multiplied by the cube of the product (1-ab)(1-a^2b^2)(1-a^3b^3)... equals the stated series 1/(1+n) + sum of (a^k/(n+a^kb^k) + b^k/(1+na^kb^k)).
